{{nihongo|'''Kinomiya Shrine'''|来宮神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

'''Kinomiya Shrine''' (きのみやじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Hatsuma, {{ill|Izu, Shizuoka|Q696840|qid=Q696840}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}.

To distinguish it from other Kinomiya Shrines, it is also called '''Hatsuma Kinomiya Shrine''' (はつま きのみやじんじゃ)<ref name="tennen">[http://www.city.izu.shizuoka.jp/gyousei/gyousei_detail000109.html City-designated Natural Monuments] - Izu City</ref>.

=== Overview ===
The shrine buildings, which had fallen into ruin, are said to have been rebuilt in the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012|lt=Jōwa}} era (1345-1349), and the shrine came to serve as the general tutelary shrine of the 16 Ōmi villages (most of the former {{ill|Nakaizu, Shizuoka|Q6960169|qid=Q6960169}} area)<ref name="tennen"/><ref name="yuisho">Precinct history board</ref>.

The pattern of a “Kinomiya Shrine” as part of {{ill|Kinomiya Faith|Q11296898|qid=Q11296898}} being brought into a place named “Hachiman” is similar to nearby {{ill|Hachimangū Kinomiya Shrine|Q11390944|qid=Q11390944}} in Yawatano, {{ill|Itō, Shizuoka|Q721163|qid=Q721163}}.

Also, in works such as ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō Dodai|Q11588823|qid=Q11588823}}'', it is named, along with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawazu Kinomiya Shrine}} (Sugihokowake-no-Mikoto Shrine) in {{ill|Kawazu, Shizuoka|Q1203861|qid=Q1203861}}, as a candidate shrine for “Sugihokowake-no-Mikoto Shrine” in the {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Izu Province|Q11380552|qid=Q11380552|lt=Shikinaisha of Izu}}. (In the northwestern nearby area, Kami-Shiraiwa, there is also {{ill|Omiya Shrine (Izu)|Q113679907|qid=Q113679907|lt=Ōmiya Shrine}}, a candidate shrine for another Shikinaisha, “Ōasa Shrine.”)

It has a distinctive landscape in which a torii and approach are formed between road and rice fields, and at the entrance to the precincts stand giant cedars designated as city natural monuments<ref name="tennen"/>.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|simple|Isotakeru-no-kami|zh|五十猛神|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto}}

=== Cultural properties ===
* Festival float (city-designated cultural property<ref>[http://www.city.izu.shizuoka.jp/gyousei/gyousei_detail000155.html City-designated crafts] - Izu City</ref>)
* Torii cedars of Hatsuma Kinomiya Shrine (city-designated natural monument<ref name="tennen"/>)

=== Festivals ===
* Annual grand festival (around October 19)

=== Access ===
* {{ill|Tokai Bus|Q11527778|qid=Q11527778}} (city-commissioned self-operated route<ref>[https://www.at-s.com/news/article/shizuoka/932289.html Route bus Nakaizu Line to be city-operated] - Shizuoka Shimbun 2021/7/21</ref>): 3-5 minutes on foot northeast from “Nakazato” or “Hatsuma” bus stops.
